Additional Small Causes Judge, Motor Accident
Claims Tribunal, Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru,
Partly Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation
And Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.

This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice C M Joshi
 Oral Judgment
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and respondent No.2.
The petitioner in MVC No.2048/2013 has approached this Court in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The factual aspect as canvassed by learned counsel appearing for the appellant is that the petitioner had sustained injuries in an accident dated 06.10.2012 involving NC: 2026:KHC:367 HC-KAR the vehicle insured by respondent No.2 and owned by respondent No.1.

In the said accident, she had suffered fracture of the left patella, abrasion over the left knee, abrasion over the left great toe, lacerated wound over the left great toe, distal phalanx and she had undergone treatment for 2 days as an inpatient.

It is submitted that she was working in Girias Electronics,
earning Rs.7,000/- per month, and was aged about 22 years.

The Tribunal, after assessing the injuries suffered by the petitioner, has awarded a sum of Rs.24,900/- towards the medical expenses,
Rs.1,719/- towards her vehicle repair bill and a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.

The tribunal also awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards the conveyance, food,
nourishment, and other expenses and rounded off the same to Rs.52,000/-.

It is submitted that the Kum.Lavanya D vs R.G.Vishwanath on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21054064/
2 said amount is on the lesser side, and as such, enhancement is required.
3.
Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent defended the impugned judgment of the Tribunal NC: 2026:KHC:367 HC-KAR and submits that the compensation awarded is adequate and proper.
4. A careful analysis of the available material on record, it may be seen that the Tribunal did not assess the compensation under the head of loss of income during the laid-up period.
Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, it could have safely be said that she was unable to resume her work for at least a period of one and a half months.
Therefore, when she has claimed her income to be Rs.7,000/- per month, it is proper to award a sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head of loss of income during the laid- up period.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal on all other heads is adequate and proper.
5. No other heads under which the compensation is available for the appellant.
Hence the appeal deserves to be allowed in part, and as such the following order is passed.
ORDER  i) The appeal is allowed in part.

NC: 2026:KHC:367 HC-KAR  ii) A sum of compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded to the petitioner in addition to the compensation awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at 6%
per annum from date of the petition till the date of depositing the amount.
iii) In the event of the deposit, entire amount be released to the petitioner.

Sd/-
